interviewQuestions.question: Explain Amdahl's Law and why throwing more cores at a problem eventually stops helping.
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
⭐ **Q: Explain Amdahl's Law and why throwing more cores at a problem eventually stops helping.**

speedup = 1 / ((1-p) + p/s), p = parallelizable fraction, s = speedup on it. As s grows large, p/s shrinks toward zero, so speedup approaches 1/(1-p) — a ceiling set by the serial fraction, regardless of processor count.

If 20% of a program is serial, best possible speedup with infinite processors is 1/0.2 = 5x. Trap: real serial fraction includes sync overhead a naive instruction count misses.

**Testing:** whether you know the ceiling is the serial fraction, and reducing it — not adding cores — is the lever.
